source_refs.note: Chapter 8 summary (PDF 119-120), with its definitions arranged as a table; paired terms share rows.

blocks.text: This chapter looked at four emerging technologies, the people and values they affect, how they can serve Pakistan, and the rules that keep them responsible. The table brings together its main terms.

blocks.caption: Chapter 8 key terms
rows: Emerging technologies
New or fast-developing technologies that can change how people live, work, communicate and solve problems
Artificial intelligence
Machines doing tasks that need human intelligence: learning, reasoning, recognising images, understanding speech, deciding
Internet of Things
Internet-connected physical devices that collect, share and act on data, e.g. smart watches, lights, cameras, soil sensors
Cloud computing
Internet-based services for storing data, running applications and using computing resources
Blockchain
Record-keeping in linked blocks, giving secure, transparent, tamper-resistant transactions
Stakeholders
People or groups affected by a technology: users, developers, organisations, governments, society
Ethical AI / bias in AI
AI that is fair, transparent, accountable, safe and responsible / unfair results from biased data, poor design or unequal representation
Inclusivity
Technology that serves people of all genders, cultures, languages, regions and backgrounds fairly
Conflict of interest
When one stakeholder's goals harm the rights, safety or interests of others
AI governance
Rules, policies and guidelines for developing and using AI responsibly
Responsible innovation
Technology that solves real problems while considering ethics, safety, culture, fairness and long-term impact
Smart agriculture / technology integration
Using IoT, AI, cloud and blockchain to improve farming / combining technologies into one more useful solution
Policy and legal frameworks
Rules and laws guiding how technologies are developed, used and controlled to protect people and society
